title: Choose the layout for Country insights
question: Same look as the rest of the portal; this choice is how the page is organised. Country first, then districts, recent years by default, district details on demand. Pick one, or re-roll.

options.label: Compare on one chart
options.thesis: The country's trend leads; districts join the same chart when you pick them, so comparison is reading one picture.
options.viewport: Country tabs with silhouettes across the top. A wide trend chart (since 2024, full record one click away) with the country line in teal; chosen districts (up to three) drawn over it in coral tones. To the right, every district as a chip with its average, highest first: tap to add it to the chart. Below: the country's figures and fishing gears.
options.risk: With three districts drawn, the chart can get busy; the district list must stay short enough to scan.

options.label: Ranked district table
options.thesis: A country header and compact trend, then every district in one ranked table; a row opens in place to show that district.
options.viewport: Country tabs; a strip of the country's figures (average, districts, fishers, boats, since) beside a compact trend. Below, the main element: all districts ranked, each row with an inline bar against the country median, latest month, a 12-month sparkline, fishers and boats. Rows re-rank in place when you switch Catch, Revenue or Price; a row opens to show the district's chart and gears.
options.risk: Table-first can read as a spreadsheet in a meeting; the bars and sparklines must carry it.

options.label: Country sheet beside the chart
options.thesis: The left column becomes the country's sheet, like the map's district sheet; click any district and the sheet turns into that district's.
options.viewport: Left column: the country drawn as an outline with coral callouts to its catch, price and revenue, then coverage and fishing gears. Right: the trend chart on top, then every district as a dot on one scale with the country median marked. Clicking a dot swaps the left sheet to that district, with a way back to the country.
options.risk: Swapping the left sheet is less obvious than an inline change; the dot scale needs labels that stay readable.
